must_fix.title: Dialog focus trap includes hidden elements (e.g. inactive TabPanels with tabIndex=0), so Shift+Tab wraps to a hidden element
must_fix.evidence: getTabbables in src/Dialog/Dialog.tsx (~lines 33-40) filters only :disabled, tabIndex<0 and hidden inputs, not hidden/inert/unrendered elements; TabPanel renders hidden panels with tabIndex={0}. Probe (Dialog with <button>first</button> + Tabs a/b, then user.tab({shift:true})) run via `pnpm vitest run src/zz_probe.test.tsx` printed `after shift-tab: DIV tabpanel hidden= true pb`. In a real browser focus() on the hidden panel does nothing and the keydown is already prevented, so Shift+Tab from the first element doesn't wrap, which breaks the issue's 'traps it there' requirement. No test covers hidden content inside the dialog.

nits: Combobox stores the active option as an index into the filtered entries, so changing `options` while the list is open moves the active option: in a probe with Apricot active, prepending 'Apex' made Apple active and Enter called onChange('a').
Tabs resolves the selected tab in a layout effect, so the first render (and renderToString) has no selected tab, every tab at tabindex=-1 and every panel hidden.
The Combobox 'No results' role=status element is only inserted when the message appears, so screen readers may not announce it; keep the live region mounted and change its text instead.

report:
I'd hold this PR for one fix: the Dialog's focus trap breaks when the dialog contains this library's own `Tabs`. Everything else holds up. `pnpm test` passes (78 tests, 3 files), `pnpm typecheck` is clean, the README matches the code, and `src/index.ts` exports what the issue asks for. There are no unrelated edits or leftover files.

**Must fix: the Dialog's focus trap sends Shift+Tab to a hidden element.** `getTabbables` in `src/Dialog/Dialog.tsx` (around lines 33–40) never excludes elements that are hidden. The library's `TabPanel` gives every panel `tabIndex={0}`, including the inactive ones that are rendered with `hidden`. With Tabs inside a Dialog, the last panel is usually hidden, and that is where Shift+Tab from the first element wraps to. To reproduce, I added a temporary probe (`src/zz_probe.test.tsx`) and deleted it afterwards:

```tsx
render(<Dialog open onOpenChange={() => {}} title="T">
  <button>first</button>
  <Tabs defaultValue="a"><TabList aria-label="x"><Tab value="a">A</Tab><Tab value="b">B</Tab></TabList>
  <TabPanel value="a">pa</TabPanel><TabPanel value="b">pb</TabPanel></Tabs>
</Dialog>);
await user.tab({ shift: true });
```

Running `pnpm vitest run src/zz_probe.test.tsx` printed:

```
start first
after shift-tab: DIV tabpanel hidden= true pb
```

In jsdom, focus lands on the hidden "B" panel. In a real browser, `focus()` on a hidden element does nothing, and the handler has already cancelled the key press. So Shift+Tab from the first element doesn't move focus at all. That breaks the issue's requirement that focus is trapped and cycles inside the dialog. The fix is to also skip elements that are hidden (`hidden`, `inert`, or not rendered), plus a test that puts Tabs inside a Dialog.

**Nits:**
- **Combobox, options changing while the list is open.** The active option is stored as a position in the filtered list, so if `options` changes while the list is open, it silently points at a different option. In a probe, Apricot was active; I then added "Apex" to the front of the list. The active option became Apple, and Enter called `onChange('a')` (Apple) instead of Apricot.
- **Tabs, first render.** No tab is selected until the layout effect runs. Under `renderToString`, both tabs have `tabindex="-1"` and both panels are `hidden`. The browser corrects this before the page paints, so it only matters for server rendering.
- **Combobox, "No results" message.** The `role="status"` element is only inserted into the page when nothing matches. Screen readers often don't announce a live region that appears at the same moment as its text.
